The pump CSV has five data rows. No upstream data or code is retained here. Additional code review on 2026-11-18 inspected integrated_agent.py and four_channel_retriever.py: use_llm=True only builds a prompt and does not invoke model_router.generate(); retriever documentation weights disagree with implementation (actual weights 0.35/0.50/0.15/0.00, so Jaccard is disabled). sources.dataOrigin: Embedded records cite GB/T/JB/T standards and generic manuals, but the exact original editions, pages, permissions and claim-to-source mapping are not established.

integrated_agent.py advertises optional LLM generation, but the reviewed use_llm branch only builds and returns a prompt; it does not call model_router.generate().
four_channel_retriever.py comments describe different channel weights from the implementation; actual weights are 0.35 vector, 0.50 equipment/symptom, 0.15 keyword and 0.00 Jaccard.
The integrated-agent prompt asks for fault causes and maintenance actions but the inspected path has no independent safety gate or source-page enforcement.

sources.title: Open-FDD — HVAC fault detection and diagnostics
sources.version: NF app VERSION 5.0.20; PyPI package pyproject 4.5.11; latest GitHub release open-fdd-v4.5.11
sources.dataLicense: not separately verified for any benchmark, demo, or telemetry data
sources.licenseStatus: MIT verified for repository code; no blanket data license established
sources.contentsReviewed: Inspected README, MIT LICENSE, VERSION, pyproject, security docs, NF app README, SQL/Pandas cookbooks, fdd-catalog.json, SQLite rule pack and representative FDD/Lite tests. The catalog contains 77 SQL rules; the cookbook lists 71 pandas twins (six SQL-only); 60 RCx charts; 52/77 rules require run-proof. Missing run proof is SKIPPED, not PASS. The rule catalog contains no per-rule source/reference fields. SQL/Pandas rules use Haystack roles, SI units, confirm windows and parity checks.
sources.dataOrigin: Repository documentation references HVAC datasets and external building/plant sources; individual source datasets and their redistribution terms were not reviewed in this pass.
sources.potentialUse: Architecture and rule-evaluation reference for HVAC FDD; next review should inspect rule equations, units, input roles, source citations and benchmark provenance.
sources.reportedScope: HVAC fault detection and diagnostics platform; current README describes SQL/Pandas rule catalogue and analytics.
sources.accessStatus: README, LICENSE, VERSION, pyproject, security docs, rule cookbooks, 77-rule catalog, SQLite pack and representative tests inspected. No external benchmark data downloaded.
qualityNotes: Strong HVAC FDD engineering: 77 SQL rules, 71 pandas equivalents, SQL/Pandas parity tests, SI-unit contract and explicit run-proof gate.
52/77 rules require run proof; absent proof yields SKIPPED rather than a false PASS. Missing time gaps are treated as unknown.
The 77-rule catalog has no per-rule source references. Rule equations, thresholds and source rights need per-rule provenance review before any transfer into our fault knowledge base.
This is rule-based HVAC fault detection/retro-commissioning, not a general industrial causal root-cause engine or calibrated RUL model.
Full NF app requires Normal Framework and Python/SQL services; Lite is a dashboard edition and does not load FDD/RCX code. Neither is a direct Android/Worker dependency.
Security docs restrict deployment to trusted LAN/VPN/OT behind NF; public unauthenticated exposure is explicitly not production-hardened. NF provides auth; app does not write field devices.
GitHub API reported pushed_at 2026-11-18T18:54:55Z, about five minutes after this run's clock; master head commit 9526665 is dated 2026-11-16T23:08Z. Treat the push timestamp as clock-skewed.
Repository VERSION is 5.0.20 while pyproject/latest release is 4.5.11; these are separate app and Python package versions, not a single release number.
sources.dataLeakage: No benchmark leakage assessment performed; any future evaluation must split by site, asset and time, not random overlapping windows.
sources.dependencies: NF app uses Normal Framework edge services, SQL.js/PGlite, Haystack model/history, Python >=3.10 package, Pandas/SQL, Docker/NF deployment. Not suitable as a direct Android or Cloudflare Worker runtime dependency.
sources.androidWorkerCompatibility: Use architecture and safety patterns only. Any rule port must be individually reviewed for source, unit, equipment scope, operating proof, confirmation time and test parity; implement a small JS subset rather than importing Python/NF services.
sources.reuseConditions: MIT verified in LICENSE for repository code. External data and third-party source rights remain separate. No wholesale rule or dataset import until each rule's provenance and scope are documented.
sources.decision: architecture-and-rule-reference-only; selective rule adaptation after per-rule source-and-safety review

sources.title: Industrial AI Troubleshooting Agent (InduQT) — boiler RAG/MCP prototype
sources.version: No tagged GitHub release; main branch last pushed 2026-09-29 and repository metadata updated 2026-11-16
sources.dataLicense: Kaggle boiler-dataset license not independently verified at the primary source; historian DB, generated alarm records, RAG documents and knowledge graph have no separately reviewed dataset/content license
sources.licenseStatus: Apache-2.0 verified for code; dataset and RAG-document rights not-yet-verified; no data redistribution permission established
sources.contentsReviewed: Reviewed the repository README, Apache-2.0 LICENSE, requirements, how_it_works, historian/alarm/RAG/knowledge-graph/tag metadata modules, boiler_kg.json, ML fault-detection script and one high-steam-temperature troubleshooting document. The prototype describes one CFB boiler, five days of 30 tags (86,400 readings), 6,005 alarm records generated from the historian with an ISA-18.2-style state machine, 62 RAG documents and 356 chunks. The sample troubleshooting document contains hard numeric limits and manual control actions without verifiable OEM source citations.
sources.dataOrigin: README points to a Kaggle 'Time Series of Industrial Boiler Operations' dataset. The exact Kaggle data license and file lineage were not independently verified at the primary source. Alarm events are generated from the same historian series; RAG documents and graph content are assembled in the repository.
sources.potentialUse: Architecture reference for historian-backed retrieval, equipment knowledge graphs, MCP tool surfaces and trace/audit design; not a reusable maintenance knowledge source.
sources.reportedScope: Single-boiler proof of concept; not a general industrial troubleshooting product or field-validated causal diagnostic engine.
sources.accessStatus: Repository and selected text files accessible and reviewed; raw DuckDB historian database was not downloaded or independently inspected; no runtime execution or model test performed.
qualityNotes: The demonstrated scope is one CFB boiler and a five-day, 30-tag time series; this is not a cross-equipment knowledge base.
The 6,005 alarm records are generated from the same historian using state-machine rules, not demonstrated as an independently sourced operator alarm log.

ml_fault_detection.py fits IsolationForest on a selected 530–545°C normal band and fits XGBoost to predict that same tag's out-of-range state from the remaining tags; no held-out evaluation is visible in the reviewed training function. This is anomaly/threshold prediction and feature ranking, not causal diagnosis.
The reviewed troubleshooting document includes exact setpoints and manual control actions without traceable OEM manual, page, revision or safety approval; do not copy or operationalize it.
The 62-document RAG corpus and 356 chunks have not been individually provenance- or license-reviewed; no text should be imported.
audit_trace.py hashes local trace files but does not provide an external signature or immutable anchor; do not describe it as tamper-proof.
sources.dataLeakage: Time-series rows are correlated; alarm labels are derived from the same historian, and the ML target is a threshold on TE_8332A. Without time-block/site/asset holdout and removal of target-derived features, random splits can leak operating regimes and produce optimistic scores.
sources.dependencies: Python 3.11, DuckDB, pandas, NumPy, scikit-learn, XGBoost, ChromaDB, sentence-transformers (~130 MB embeddings), NetworkX and MCP; README reports roughly 1.5 GB of dependencies and a Claude Code workflow.
sources.androidWorkerCompatibility: Not suitable as a direct Android or Cloudflare Worker dependency. Use only architecture ideas; the Python/MCP, DuckDB, vector-store and model stack is too heavy for the current mobile-first local runtime.
sources.reuseConditions: Apache-2.0 applies to repository code with its notices. Do not reuse the Kaggle dataset copy, alarm DB, RAG documents, numeric thresholds or control actions until each upstream file's rights, provenance, source page and safety review are established.
